title: Queso Fundido with Salsa Verde
notes: Any combination of these cheeses or herbs can be found used in queso fundido variations throughout Mexico. Explore different combinations to find your favourite. If you have a good quality "molcajete," a volcanic rock mortar or bowl, it will keep the cheese hot and melted. However, a good heavy non-stick or cast iron pan that is all metal and can go in the oven is almost as good. A small porcelain casserole dish or large ramekin will work too. In any case, check that the volume of cheese matches the size of the dish before starting.

ingredientSections.heading: Queso Fundido
items: 2-3 Cups Mozzarella, soft Manchego or Edam
½ Cup Gruyere or Emmental (or Raclette if you want something milder)
2 Tbsp of your favourite herb: basil, oregano, thyme

methodSections.heading: Salsa Verde
steps: Peel then cut the tomatillos in half, cut the serrano pepper in half and quarter the onion.
Place all ingredients in a saucepan and top with just enough water to cover them.
Place a lid on the saucepan, bring to a boil and then remove from the heat, but leave covered for a few minutes to allow the tomatillos to finish settling and the temperature to cool off a little.
Blend everything together until smooth and check the seasoning. Add a little more salt if necessary.

methodSections.heading: Queso Fundido
steps: Coarsely grate the cheese, finely chop the herbs and mix all together in a bowl.
If using a molcajete or a cast iron dish, place it on a small oven safe tray and preheat in the oven set to 200°C (400°F) for at least 15 minutes.
If using a porcelain or ceramic ramekin there is no need to preheat.
Tranfer the cheese mixture into the baking dish, and place in the oven at 200°C (400°F) for 10 minutes.
Carefully remove from the oven and bring the outside edges into the centre with a spoon to make sure it melts evenly. Place back in the oven.
Check every 5 minutes and mix with a spoon again when necessary. It will be done when the centre feels very soft and the top begins to take on a nice golden brown colour.
While the cheese is in the oven, heat up the half cup of salsa verde.
Remove the cheese from the oven carefully and place on a heat safe pad. Pour the hot salsa verde over the top of the cheese and add a few sprigs of cilantro.
Serve with tortillas or chips right away; it will not stay melted long enough to wait on anyone and cheese does not like to be re-melted!
